automations.name: New Inquiry Welcome
automations.summary: When someone calls, fills out your website form or submits a Facebook lead form, they’re added to your lead board, assigned to your patient coordinator, and sent a thank-you email and text right away.
glance: Someone calls, submits your website form or a Facebook lead form
A notification about the new inquiry
Right after the thank-you text, when follow-up (automation 2) begins

steps.title: Someone contacts your practice
steps.body: Starts when a new lead comes in from a phone call, your website form or a Facebook lead form.
steps.note: All of these automations are in Draft in GHL, so nothing is being sent yet. They go live once you approve.

steps.title: The inquiry is added to your lead board
steps.body: A New Lead card is created on your Marketing Pipeline and assigned to your patient coordinator (currently Calvin). Your team gets a notification.
steps.note: If this person is already an active patient, or is already being followed up, no welcome messages go out. Your team is alerted instead so nobody gets a duplicate welcome.

steps.title: Email: Thank you for contacting us

email.subject: Thank you for contacting [Practice name]
email.body:
Hello,

Thank you for reaching out to [Practice name]. We've received your inquiry, and a member of our patient care team will contact you shortly to learn about your goals and answer any questions.

If you'd like to speak with us sooner, please call [Main phone] during office hours ([Office hours]).

Every consultation with [Doctor name] begins with a private, unhurried conversation about what matters to you. There's never any pressure, just thoughtful guidance.

Warm regards,
The Patient Care Team
[Practice name]

For your privacy, please don't reply with medical details or photos. If we need information from you, we'll send a secure link.

[Practice name] · [Office address] · [Main phone]

steps.title: Text: Thank you for reaching out
steps.sms: Hello from [Practice name]. Thank you for reaching out to our office. A patient coordinator will follow up with you shortly. Questions in the meantime? Call [Main phone]. Reply STOP to opt out.
steps.note: Texts only go out 9am–7pm Eastern, Monday–Saturday. If this step is reached outside those hours, the text waits until the window opens.

steps.title: The lead moves to Attempting Contact
steps.body: This starts the follow-up calls, texts and emails in automation 2.

steps.title: Done
steps.body: Follow-up continues in automation 2.

questions.text: Who should new inquiries be assigned to?
questions.why: Every new lead is currently assigned to Calvin.

questions.text: Are the office hours shown in the first email correct?
questions.why: The email shows [Office hours] from your account settings.

questions.text: Is 9am–7pm Eastern, Monday–Saturday the right window for texts?
questions.why: Texts reached outside this window wait until it opens.

automations.name: Follow-Up Until We Reach Them
automations.summary: For new inquiries we haven’t spoken with yet. Over 14 days your team gets call reminders while the patient receives a few short texts and emails. It stops as soon as they reply or your team connects with them.
glance: A new inquiry moves to Attempting Contact
When they reply, your team connects with them, or on day 15 if we never reach them

steps.title: A new inquiry moves to Attempting Contact
steps.body: Starts right after the welcome messages in automation 1.

steps.title: Call reminder 1: First call
steps.body: Your team gets a task to call now, confirm their interest and find out which area they’re interested in. If they reach the patient, they move the card to Connected / Qualifying, and the follow-up stops.

steps.title: Text 1: Following up
steps.sms: Hi, this is [Practice name] following up on your recent inquiry. When is a good time for a quick call? You can also reach us at [Main phone]. Reply STOP to opt out.
steps.note: Texts only go out 9am–7pm Eastern, Monday–Saturday. If this step is reached outside those hours, the text waits until the window opens.

steps.title: Call reminder 2
steps.body: A second call attempt.

steps.title: Email 1: Following up on your inquiry

email.subject: Following up on your inquiry
email.body:
Hello,

We wanted to follow up on your recent inquiry with [Practice name]. Whenever you're ready, we'd be glad to answer your questions and help you find a consultation time that fits your schedule.

Simply reply to this email with a good time to reach you, or call us at [Main phone].

Warm regards,
The Patient Care Team
[Practice name]

For your privacy, please don't reply with medical details or photos. If we need information from you, we'll send a secure link.

[Practice name] · [Office address] · [Main phone]

steps.title: Call reminder 3
steps.body: A third call attempt.

steps.title: Text 2: Just checking in
steps.sms: [Practice name] here, just checking in. Would a morning or afternoon call work better for you? Reply with a time and we'll do our best to make it work.

steps.title: Email 2: What to expect at a consultation

email.subject: What to expect at a consultation
email.body:
Hello,

Many people tell us they weren't sure what a first consultation would be like, so here's a quick look:

A private conversation. You'll meet with [Doctor name] to talk through your goals and questions.

Personal guidance. Every recommendation is tailored to you. There is no one-size-fits-all plan.

A dedicated coordinator. Our patient care team helps with scheduling, planning and any questions along the way.

If you'd like to set up a time, reply to this email or call [Main phone].

Warm regards,
The Patient Care Team
[Practice name]

For your privacy, please don't reply with medical details or photos. If we need information from you, we'll send a secure link.

[Practice name] · [Office address] · [Main phone]

steps.title: Call reminder 4
steps.body: A fourth call attempt.

steps.title: Text 3: Here when you’re ready
steps.sms: Hi from [Practice name]. We're happy to help whenever you're ready. Just reply here or call [Main phone].

steps.title: Email 3: We’ll be here when you’re ready

email.subject: We'll be here when you're ready
email.body:
Hello,

We haven't been able to connect, so we'll pause our follow-up for now. We don't want to fill your inbox.

If you'd like to talk in the future, reply to this email or call [Main phone]. We'd be glad to hear from you.

Warm regards,
The Patient Care Team
[Practice name]

For your privacy, please don't reply with medical details or photos. If we need information from you, we'll send a secure link.

[Practice name] · [Office address] · [Main phone]

steps.title: Text 4: Pausing our follow-up
steps.sms: [Practice name] here. We'll pause our follow-up for now. If you'd like to connect later, just reply or call [Main phone]. We're here when you're ready.

steps.title: Final call reminder
steps.body: One last call attempt. If there’s still no answer, the card is closed tomorrow.

steps.title: Closed as Lost (Unresponsive)
steps.body: If they’re still in Attempting Contact, the card is closed as Lost. They’ll get one gentle check-in 90 days later (automation 10).

steps.title: Done
steps.body: The follow-up stops early as soon as the person replies or your team moves them forward.

questions.text: Is 14 days of follow-up the right length?
questions.why: After day 14 we stop contacting them.

questions.text: Should leads we never reach be closed as Lost on day 15?
questions.why: Closing them keeps your lead board current. They still get a check-in after 90 days.
options: No, leave them open for the team to decide

questions.text: Is this the right number of calls?
questions.why: Your team gets 5 call reminders over 14 days.

automations.name: Behind the Scenes
automations.summary: These run in the background to keep your lead board accurate and alert your team. Patients don’t receive anything from them. We’re showing them so you know what your team will see.

steps.title: Background automations
steps.body: These help your team. None of them send anything to patients.

steps.when: When a routing tag is added
steps.title: The lead is routed to the right pipeline
steps.body: When your team tags a lead as Surgical, BII / Explant or Non-Surgical, their card moves to that pipeline at Qualified and intake follow-up stops. If they’ve already booked in another area, nothing moves and your team gets a task to review it.

steps.when: When a procedure tag is added
steps.title: Procedure categories are kept in sync
steps.body: Procedure tags are grouped into categories (for example Breast, Body, Injectables, Laser) so reporting and rebook timing work.

steps.title: Reminder to classify the lead
steps.body: If a connected lead still has no routing tag after 24 hours, your team gets a task and a notification.

steps.title: Your team is told when a patient replies
steps.body: Any reply by text or email sends a notification and a task to reply. STOP replies and spam are skipped.

steps.title: Stale lead alert
steps.body: If a card sits for 7 days with no activity, your coordinator gets a task and a notification.

steps.when: When a lead contacts you again
steps.title: Returning leads are reopened
steps.body: If someone who was closed calls or submits a form again, their existing card reopens instead of a duplicate being created, and your team is notified.

steps.when: When a contact is tagged as spam
steps.title: Spam clean-up
steps.body: The card is closed as Spam / Wrong Number and all follow-up stops.

questions.text: Who should get the stale-lead and patient-replied alerts?
